title: Gardener Brutally Beaten by Homeless Man Outside Brentwood Home, Neighbors Demand Action - NewsBreak
text: BRENTWOOD - A gardener working outside a Brentwood home was violently attacked by a homeless man on Monday, in what neighbors are calling a terrifying escalation of ongoing safety concerns tied to a nearby vacant property. The victim, identified as Rodolfo Roman, was tending to a residence on the 11900 block of Dorothy Street on June 23 when a shirtless man approached, shouting about the noise from Roman's lawn equipment. According to a report by KTLA, the man then raised a large stick and began beating Roman in the head and face, continuing the assault even after Roman fell to the ground. Roman, who attempted to shield himself, suffered a broken arm and a deep gash to his head that required staples. He was later hospitalized. "I was very scared," Roman told KTLA's Jennifer McGraw. "My legs were shaking and I'm down on the ground." The suspect, whose identity has not been released, was taken into custody by Los Angeles police on Tuesday evening near Bundy Drive and Santa Monica Boulevard in the Sawtelle neighborhood. Brentwood residents say the attack is the latest in a string of incidents linked to an abandoned home near the site of the assault. The house, which burned down over a decade ago, has become a magnet for squatters and criminal activity, according to neighbors. Sean Heffron, who lives next door to the abandoned property, said the neighborhood has repeatedly reported dangerous conditions to city officials with no resolution. "He hits him while he's down, without conscience and at full strength," Heffron said of the attacker. Neighbors told KTLA that fires, break-ins, and disturbances have become commonplace at the vacant site.
